May 2026 Fuel and New-Energy Passenger-Vehicle Sales Lists
evidence_excerpt: The association reports May domestic retail of 1.04 million units for Chinese brands, down 17% year on year, with a 68.7% share, up 3.8 percentage points. Mainstream joint-venture retail was 0.31 million, down 35%; luxury retail was 0.16 million, down 20%.

The same association source reports May factory wholesale of 1.663 million units for Chinese brands, up 4%, versus 0.336 million for mainstream joint ventures, down 29%, and 0.213 million for luxury brands, down 12%.

A B-tier industry source reports that nine of the top ten fuel passenger-vehicle models were Chinese brands in May; this is used as a cross-check for competitive context, not as a concentration metric.
scope_and_caliber: Mainland China passenger vehicles in May 2026. Brand-bloc data comes from the association source. The project workbook has no complete brand mapping or CR5 field, so model-level brand concentration must not be calculated.
metric_value_and_unit: Chinese-brand retail: 1.04 million units, -17% YoY, 68.7% share, +3.8 percentage points
Mainstream joint-venture retail: 0.31 million units, -35% YoY
Luxury retail: 0.16 million units, -20% YoY, 10.6% share, +0.2 percentage points
metric_type: Association brand-bloc retail and wholesale statistics; not a complete brand-by-model concentration database.
contribution_or_rank_change: Chinese-brand domestic retail share rose 3.8 percentage points year on year. The source provides no project-ready brand CR5 or model-to-brand table.
segment_definition: Chinese brands, mainstream joint ventures and luxury brands are association-defined blocs. The deep-analysis source explicitly defines its luxury-brand coverage; individual brand membership should follow that source before aggregation.
structure_change: Chinese brands lost retail volume less severely than mainstream joint ventures and increased share, while luxury retail also declined in volume but had a marginal share increase.
representative_models: TOP15 examples are maintained in the separate top15_model_movements item. This item avoids inferring whole-brand performance from a single model.
lifecycle_event: [uncertain] No complete brand product-calendar, dealer-policy or channel-coverage dataset was collected for brand-bloc causality.
overall_judgement: May competition is defined by relative resilience rather than broad market growth: Chinese brands maintained a much larger retail share because their decline was less severe than mainstream joint ventures. This supports a brand-bloc competitive shift, but it does not establish CR5, individual-brand profitability or the reason for each bloc's movement.
observed_fact: Chinese-brand retail declined 17% year on year with a 68.7% share, while mainstream joint-venture retail declined 35%. Chinese-brand wholesale grew 4% while mainstream joint-venture wholesale declined 29%.
causal_mechanism: A slower decline in Chinese-brand retail mechanically raises its market share versus a faster-declining joint-venture bloc. Product breadth and electrification may be explanations, but the current evidence does not quantify their contribution or isolate them from exports, inventory and pricing.
confidence_level: High for association brand-bloc facts; medium for the relative-share interpretation; low for individual-brand and causal conclusions.
alternative_explanations: Different product cycles, powertrain mix, regional coverage, dealer inventory, export allocation, fleet volume, discounting and brand definitions may affect the measured brand-bloc changes.
competitive_set: Chinese brands, mainstream joint ventures and luxury brands at market level; individual model competition must be assessed in the corresponding category, class and powertrain.
competitive_advantage_or_barrier: The evidence indicates relative share resilience for Chinese brands, not a universal advantage. Brand-specific advantages in cost, technology, channel or software require separate evidence.
configuration_threshold: [uncertain] No common configuration threshold can be inferred from brand-bloc statistics.
pricing_and_profit_signal: The association source notes dealer operating pressure and inventory adjustment but does not provide comparable brand transaction prices, rebates or profits.
target_user_segment: [uncertain] Brand-bloc data does not identify buyer personas or purchase occasions.
purchase_motivation_and_pain_points: [uncertain] Customer research is needed before stating why a buyer selected a Chinese brand, joint venture or luxury brand.
purchase_barrier: [uncertain] Availability, service coverage, financing, resale value and perceived technology risk are not measured in this dataset.
channel_signal: Track brand-bloc and individual-brand retail, wholesale, dealer stock, transaction price, finance approval and order conversion separately, with the same brand-definition dictionary.
opportunity_or_risk_grade: B competitive signal for Chinese-brand share resilience; C watch for joint-venture pressure. No individual-brand market-entry grade is issued.
recommended_action: Use brand-bloc statistics as context for competitive positioning, then connect only verified TOP15 model movements and product events to the page-level market explanation. Do not generate CR5 or brand concentration without a complete brand mapping.
regional_capacity_or_channel_action: Set regional actions only after measuring brand-bloc movement by province/city tier and dealer network. National share gains do not prove regional capacity needs.
decision_condition_and_trigger: Escalate a brand-bloc signal into strategy only when retail-share, price/discount, product pipeline and channel conversion evidence align across at least two months.
next_verification: Build a model-to-brand master table and join it to monthly sales, powertrain, MSRP, transaction price, inventory, region, dealer and export data; then calculate concentration on a declared scope.
data_quality_status: Passed for association brand-bloc facts; incomplete for brand concentration, brand-model mapping, price and profitability.
data_gap_or_conflict: The business workbook has no complete brand mapping or CR5. External lists use their own model aggregation and scope, so they cannot be directly merged without a reconciliation key.
claim_boundary: This item can state relative brand-bloc volume and share movement. It cannot state that a particular brand, technology, price action or channel policy caused the shift.
